human_tolerance.notes: Wild wetland bird; this contribution makes no claim of garden use.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Northern pintails winter in Mexico and breed farther north; this period marks their broad migration absence from the wintering range.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: The species breeds in the north-central United States; this broad window follows the source account and does not resolve local variation.

vocalizations.description: Male gives a soft flute-like whistle; female gives a descending quack. This call represents the species generally.

taxonomy.note: Both providers resolve accepted species Anas acuta at species rank; GBIF key 2498112 and ITIS TSN 175074 checked 2026-10-31.

external.note: GBIF key 2498112 is accepted species Anas acuta; iNaturalist taxon 6933 is active species Anas acuta.

range.note: North America native range: breeds in Alaska, Canada and the north-central US; winters farther south in the US and Mexico. US query is a seasonal/nonbreeding and breeding range, not a single resident population.

traits.body_plan.note: Bird; bipedal, feathered, endothermic, lung-breathing, powered flight; structural convention judgement.

traits.limb_count.note: Two legs; wings are not counted as limbs in this schema.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walking, swimming and powered flight are supported by the source descriptions.

traits.nest_type.note: Ground scrape concealed in vegetation, often away from water.

traits.perching.note: Judgement: waterfowl are not represented as perching.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Feeds mainly evening or night; spends much of day resting.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: takes flight to escape terrestrial predators.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement; no numerical wariness estimate found.

traits.size_class.note: Medium duck; derived from adult female and male mass ranges (0.45–1.36 kg) and schema size classes.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of combined reported adult mass range 450–1360 g, converted to 0.905 kg. This is a range midpoint, not a measured population mean.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Combined reported male/female adult ranges: 450–1360 g; converted to kg.

traits.length_m.note: Combined reported adult length range 51–76 cm; midpoint converted to 0.635 m.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Reported wingspan 80–95 cm; midpoint converted to 0.875 m.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Approximation from adult annual survival at one Alaska banding site: 1 + mean of p/(1-p) for males (0.776) and females (0.602) = 3.49 years. Conditional adult-survivor estimate, not all-age mean; local survival may differ.

traits.diet.note: Authored broad annual allocation for the simulation: seeds/plant material dominate outside breeding; invertebrates increase in breeding season. Shares are model weights, not measured proportions.

traits.social.note: Pair breeding and large nonbreeding flocks; group-size bounds are judgement.

habitat.use.note: Authored split reflecting shallow open wetlands, terrestrial grain feeding and flight; proportions are not measured.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Open water / wetland resting habitat; water is a simulation shelter proxy.

habitat.resources.note: Plants/seeds and aquatic invertebrates; resources modeled for dabbling, swimming and ground nesting.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Authored neutral outdoor-wildlife values; no sourced urban affinity estimate.

seasonal.strategy.note: Migratory; North American birds breed north and winter farther south. US includes both parts of the annual range.

seasonal.phases.note: Omitted because a single month window would merge distinct US breeding, passage and winter populations; the source describes regional migration but does not support one national calendar.

look.note: Block-model colours and proportions are authored from the male chocolate head, white neck stripe/breast, grey body and pointed tail; female mottled brown variation is not represented.

behavior.note: Authored local duck program. Walks on shore, swims while feeding, flies when alarmed; rests in daylight and feeds at night. Dabbling/upending is not explicitly animated.

conservation.note: IUCN Least Concern reported; conservation status is not a population trend claim.

vocalizations.call.note: Male described as soft flute-like whistle; female as descending quack. One general contact call approximation.

seasonal.life_stages.note: The juvenile duration is 46-47 days to fledging; Egg and Adult are life-stage labels.
